name: HVAC Contractors
purpose: AhernAI sales discovery and illustrative configuration guidance
summary: For heating and cooling businesses; clarify service, maintenance or installation and residential versus commercial work. Explore routine office tasks without equipment advice or emergency-response promises. Ask one useful question at a time about the caller's actual workflow. Explain Level 1 when messages and FAQs fit; move directly to Level 2 when the caller needs routine work completed. Recommend the lowest suitable level as soon as the need is understood; no mandatory three-level tour. Introduce Level 3 only when the caller asks about it, requests all three levels, or raises employee coordination, supervisory duties or difficult/disgruntled callers. Routine order-taking, scheduling, CRM work or the number of connected tools does not trigger a Manager upsell.
discovery_questions: What kind of heating and cooling work makes up most of your business?
Which calls are hardest to keep up with during your busy periods?
How are new service requests handled when your office is unavailable?
What information must the office have before deciding whether to accept a job?
Are maintenance visits bookable directly, or does every request need dispatch review?
Which system holds your appointments or customer records?
Which complaints or policy questions still need your personal attention?

levels.name: Answering Service
use_cases: Answer questions about hours, service areas and offered services using approved descriptions.
Collect contact details, location and the caller's service, maintenance or replacement inquiry without diagnosing equipment.
Send a clear request summary to one agreed destination so office staff can prioritize callbacks under their own rules.
levels.probe: Would a complete callback summary solve the biggest issue when calls arrive faster than your team can answer?
fit_signals: The main need is capturing requests during busy periods.
A human dispatcher should retain all scheduling decisions.

levels.name: Receptionist
use_cases: Qualify service requests using approved service areas and request categories, and offer screened transfers when a person is needed.
Book or reschedule eligible maintenance and consultation appointments, and update the agreed customer or job system through the included receptionist automation.
Route approved service details to the office or dispatch intake queue; respect any human review required before technician assignment.
levels.probe: Which maintenance or service requests can be booked under your normal office rules?
fit_signals: The caller needs routine receptionist work completed rather than only a message.
Approved business rules and verified systems support the agreed workflow.

levels.name: Manager
use_cases: Gather detailed complaints about a previous visit and the caller's requested resolution for human review, without diagnosing the reported problem.
Explain approved appointment, maintenance-plan or follow-up policies without inventing entitlements, warranty coverage or financial remedies.

Support approved employee coordination, such as recording a shift callout or coverage request and routing it to the authorized supervisor. Employment, staffing approval, disciplinary, financial and policy-exception decisions remain human; do not request medical reasons or other sensitive employee details.
levels.probe: Only after the caller raises a management need: Which situations should the agent handle under approved rules, and which should reach you?
fit_signals: The caller asks for help with difficult or disgruntled callers and escalations.
The caller wants approved employee coordination or supervisory support.

scope_boundaries: No equipment diagnosis, DIY repair, electrical or gas instructions, warranty determinations or promised emergency service. Do not equate message capture or booking with dispatch or a guaranteed arrival.

If the caller raises an immediate safety concern, stop sales discovery and refer at a high level to appropriate local emergency services or a qualified human; provide no hazard troubleshooting or medical claims.
Refunds, credits, discounts, policy exceptions and technical judgments remain with humans. No live booking, transfer, notification or other action is established by these illustrative examples.

Level 1 captures approved FAQs, caller details and a summary to one destination; it does not book, submit orders, update a CRM or make screened transfers. Level 2 covers agreed routine receptionist duties and supporting automation. Package fit is based on duties, not a one-calendar/one-CRM or two-integration quota. Scope is agreed before launch; this is not an unlimited software-development commitment.

Routine receptionist duties and the supporting automation are included in the agreed Level 2 scope, without an additional AhernAI automation or integration-build charge. Confirm software compatibility, access, allowed actions and failure handling during setup; an unverified connection is not an automatic surcharge.

Introduce Level 3 only when the caller asks about it, requests all three levels, or raises employee coordination, supervisory duties or difficult/disgruntled callers. Routine order-taking, scheduling, CRM work or the number of connected tools does not trigger a Manager upsell.

Do not promise that a named app or POS is supported merely because the caller names it. Verify compatibility during setup and agree a workable destination or fallback; disclose any actual work outside the agreed duties before proceeding.
setup_requirements: Confirm accepted work, service area, hours, approved FAQs, maintenance-policy wording and one summary destination.
Document booking versus dispatch-review rules, allowed slots, after-hours human coverage and escalation or unavailable-recipient behavior.
Confirm selected systems, application compatibility and allowed workflow actions; test normal requests, out-of-scope requests and failed handoffs before launch.
Agree the routine duties and supporting automation included in the package, approved actions, access permissions, successful completion signals and failure paths before launch.

adjacent_services.trigger: The business needs broader back-office work beyond its agreed receptionist duties.
adjacent_services.example: Explore a separate project only for that broader need. Automation needed for agreed Level 2 receptionist work is already included; do not resell it as a Quickstart or add-on.

adjacent_services.trigger: The owner describes unclear online service information or an ineffective inquiry form.
adjacent_services.example: Explore a website update around the desired visitor action and agreed follow-up process.
